page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / The Crisis
title: The Crisis
description:
Denise explains why she's in such a state of panic and Paul is not pleased. Will Anna be able to help resolve the crisis?
This episode explores language for making suggestions.
phrases: Have you tried asking your colleagues?
Maybe I could do a big office search for you...?
How about looking through your rubbish bin...?

listening_challenge.question: Why was the memory stick wet?
listening_challenge.answer: Because it had been in Paul’s tea.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Here we are again at Tip Top Trading, where Anna's interview for a sales job has been suddenly interrupted. Office assistant Denise has entered the room, looking very worried. What's wrong? And will Anna have any suggestions that might help?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: I don't know what to do!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: So what's the matter Denise?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: You know the PowerPoint presentation?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: The one we've been preparing for the last two months?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: The one that's very, very important and that we need this afternoon?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: That one.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Aha.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: We've lost everything!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: No!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: I had it on a USB stick, to transfer it, but the stick has vanished!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
Right Anna, now is your chance to help them find solutions to the problem.
You'll need phrases like:

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: But don't you have it saved on your computer?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: No, it was taking up a lot of space, so I deleted it.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: So you have lost the only copy we have.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: What idiots! I've never seen such a disorganised office. Go on, you'd better help them, Anna.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Can I make a suggestion?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes, please do!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Why don't you try looking in your recycle bin? It might still be there.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: I did. It isn't.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Have you tried asking your colleagues if they've seen the memory stick?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: I did. They haven't.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text:
How about looking through your rubbish bin to see if you threw it away by mistake?

Denise
(getting shirty) I don't do silly things like that!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: All very sensible suggestions Anna, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Maybe I could do a big office search for you...? I'm good at finding things.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: There are confidential documents in this office – non-staff are not allowed to see them.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Now, now Denise. Why don't you drink up that nice tea?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I have an idea! Did you ever email the presentation to anyone?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Golly gosh, you did Denise! You emailed it to me to proof-read. It'll be in my inbox somewhere. Good thinking Anna!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: I was just about to suggest that myself.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Problem solved. Thank you Anna!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Pleasure.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well done Anna!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Right, now please leave us Denise. Anna and I will continue our interview. Would you like a biscuit Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thank you. Oh, what's that?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text:
Oh golly gosh, the USB stick! It was mixed in with the plate of biscuits that Denise brought in.

Anna
It's wet

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes, I think maybe I stirred my tea with it at one point. Oh well. Now, where were we...? My goodness, it's 11 o'clock! I have a meeting right now! I'm afraid I'm going to have to go. But I've made my mind up about you anyway. I suppose you'd like to know if you've got the job?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes please!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Ah - Stop right there! I'm sure everybody would like to know if Anna's got the job – but everybody's going to have to wait until we've heard her helpful phrases once again:

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Anna, we need someone who can think on her feet and who is a first-rate people person. Someone who sees solutions, not problems... someone like you! So if you want the job, it's yours!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Ah, now think carefully Anna – do you really want to work for these people? They seem a bit... disorganised.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I would definitely like the job! Thank you!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: So be it. Join us again next week for Anna's first day as a sales executive at Tip Top Trading.
